Thanks Marissa — great demo. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 6,000 parallel request figure is a peak during marketing bursts. Typical steady peaks are closer to 2,500 concurrent requests.
- We use long-lived HTTP/2 connections from our edge (connection pooling across 50 app servers). We'd prefer Redwood to support multiplexed streams over those connections and not require reconnects for each request.
- For streaming: we want token-by-token flush so our UI can render progressively; ideally chunk sizes of 128 tokens or smaller with low flush latency.
- On throttling: we cannot accept sudden 429s for user-facing requests. Graceful backpressure or queueing with explicit retry windows is preferred.

We're available Friday 10–11am PT for the sync. Tom from infra will join to confirm connection topology.

Quick tech notes to prep for Friday: 

- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 with token-by-token flush. Flush latency is typically <30ms per chunk on Dedicated pools; we can tune chunk size and buffer thresholds.
- Connection pooling: we support long-lived HTTP/2 connections from client edge. Our gateway keeps multiplexed streams; you can keep 50 app servers with persistent connections. We don't require reconnects per request.
- Concurrency model: we track both in-flight parallel requests and per-connection stream count. For quotaing we expose two knobs: concurrent_request_limit and streaming_stream_limit. For your worst-case 6k parallel requests, we'd recommend a Dedicated capacity pool with a baseline quota of 4k concurrent requests and a burst allowance of +2k tied to capacity autoscaling.
- Backpressure: we prefer returning 503 with Retry-After for non-user-critical batch workloads and soft-queueing for interactive sessions; for user-facing requests we can configure graceful queuing (max queue time + immediate fallback to lighter model).

I'll bring a sample rate-limits table and a proposal for Dedicated pool sizing. Attaching the proposal PDF.

Laura Bennett

Thanks everyone for the alignment on Friday. Summary + proposed next steps: 

Summary of agreed baseline:
- Baseline Dedicated pool sized for 4,000 concurrent requests (covers steady peaks).
- Burst policy: +2,000 concurrent slot burst tied to autoscaling (30-minute cool down, subject to capacity).
- Streaming: token-by-token flush supported; default chunk target 64–128 tokens, flush latency target <50ms.
- Connection pooling: support long-lived HTTP/2 with multiplexing; no per-request reconnects required.
- Backpressure policy: graceful queueing for interactive requests up to 3s, fallback to smaller model on exceeding queue threshold; non-critical batch jobs receive 503 + Retry-After.

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) Redwood to provide formal quota table & pricing for the baseline + burst config (Marissa) — see attached proposal.
2) ACME infra to confirm exact edge connection counts and TLS termination (Tom) — due EOD Mon.
3) Procurement to review SOW and lead time and confirm PO timeline (procurement@acme.com).
4) Schedule a 2-week pilot starting once PO received; pilot success metric: sustained 95th p99 latency <= 600ms for 128-token requests under 70% of tested peak traffic.

Marissa will follow up with an updated proposal and a DocuSign-ready quote once Tom confirms connection counts.
